analysis_input.complaint_verbatim:
Listen:
"cust has had a payment to wix taken out 18/12 £604.80
cust did not want this payment leaving
cust had a fraud block on the 14/12 - we had blocked the payment - cancelled her card - secured the acc

cust has now called to stated that we have not followed her instructions of not allowing the payment to through
the payment has gone through which was originally stopped on the 14/12
cust has been misinformed - no payments to be leaving to that merch
on the call cust asked if there was anything else she needed to do - we advised nothing further
had we told cust that she needed to follow this up with wix - she would have - no mention of cpa
the bank has given out her new card details to wix
bank did not ask for cust approval like it did on the 14/12
bank has breached on multiple accounts
cust is very unhappy about all this
has been on call for over 2hrs

wants refund for the amount
wants to know who else is set up for cpa"

fact_find_output.complaint_summary:
1. What is the customer unhappy about?
    - £604.80 payment to Wix taken on 18/12 despite a fraud block on 14/12.
    - Organisation did not follow instructions to prevent the payment.
    - Misinformation provided, advising nothing further needed after 14/12 call.
    - Organisation did not inform customer to follow up with Wix regarding CPA.
    - Organisation gave new card details to Wix.
    - Organisation did not ask for customer approval for the payment, unlike on 14/12.
    - Organisation breached on multiple accounts.
2. What is the impact on the customer?
    - £604.80 payment taken.
    - Over 2 hours on call.
    - Very unhappy.
3. What does the customer want us to do to fix the issue?
    - Refund for £604.80.
    - Information on who else is set up for CPA.
    - To speak to a Team Manager.
    - To be called or emailed.
4. What actions has the organisation taken so far?
    - Apologised and empathised.
    - Explained no CPA was placed and payment was not taken as CPA.
    - Explained payment would still leave account even if CPA was placed.
    - Explained Visa, not organisation, gave Wix card details.
    - Explained payment taken as credential on file.
    - Explained nothing further could have been done on 14/12 call.
    - Explained how to check CPA.
    - Offered £40 D&I.
    - Advised to raise as a dispute and prepare info.
    - Escalated the complaint as customer not accepting outcome.
    - Looked into previous fraud cases.
    - Looked into how the payment was taken.
5. Additional relevant information:
    - Customer had previous dealings with Wix, making a payment in 2021 for £100 odd.
    - Customer mentioned speaking to Wix.
    - Team Manager advised escalation.
6. Timeline of events:
    - 2021: Customer made a payment to Wix for £100 odd.
    - 14/12: Fraud block placed, payment blocked, card cancelled, account secured.
    - 18/12: £604.80 payment to Wix taken out.
    - 08/01/2026: FPI OCEAN BAY HOLIDAY (specific date not provided)

tables.title: Complaint transactions assessed for quick succession

layer_3_method.rationale: This check identifies whether complaint transactions were made in quick succession — a pattern that can indicate fraud or coercion. Transactions are assessed against two timeframes: hourly and weekly.
rules: We look at all complaint transactions in chronological order and group them based on how close together they are
Hourly clusters: 3 or more payments where each payment is within 1 hour of the previous one
Weekly clusters: 4 or more payments where each payment is within 7 days of the previous one
A transaction can appear in both an hourly and a weekly cluster, as the two checks run independently

thresholds.hourly: At least 3 payments within 1 hour; if more follow, each must be no more than 1 hour after the last
thresholds.weekly: At least 4 payments within 7 days; if more follow, each must be no more than 7 days after the last

layer_3_method.rationale: This check identifies whether the complaint transaction was made a time of day when the customer rarely or never makes payments. We look at the transaction history with the lookback window to understand when this customer typically transacts, then show any complaint transaction that falls outside their normal active hours.
rules: We analyse all of the customer's transactions over the past 13 months to build a picture of when they normally make payments throughout the day
We smooth this picture so that nearby times of day are treated similarly. For example, if a customer is active at 10:00, they are also considered active at 10:15
Activity around midnight is treated as continuous, so a customer active at 23:30 is also considered active at 00:15
Each complaint transaction is checked against this profile - if it was made during a time of day where the customer has very little or no history of transacting, it is shown as unusual

thresholds.unusual: A transaction is flagged if it falls in a time period that accounts for less than ~1% of the customer's historical activity
thresholds.note: Exact threshold is subject to calibration during testing

- £604.80 payment to Wix taken on 18/12 despite a fraud block on 14/12.
- Organisation did not follow instructions to prevent the payment.
- Misinformation provided, advising nothing further needed after 14/12 call.
- Organisation did not inform customer to follow up with Wix regarding CPA.
- Organisation gave new card details to Wix.
- Organisation did not ask for customer approval for the payment, unlike on 14/12.

3. What does the customer want us to do to fix the issue?
- Information on who else is set up for CPA.
- To speak to a Team Manager.

- Explained no CPA was placed and payment was not taken as CPA.
- Explained payment would still leave account even if CPA was placed.
- Explained Visa, not organisation, gave Wix card details.

- Explained nothing further could have been done on 14/12 call.
- Advised to raise as a dispute and prepare info.
- Escalated the complaint as customer not accepting outcome.
- Looked into how the payment was taken.
- Customer had previous dealings with Wix, making a payment in 2021 for £100 odd.
